questions.q: What traditions are important in your family?
questions.answer: Respecting elders is central, so we greet older relatives formally and seek their blessings at Eid. We also make pitha, traditional rice cakes, in winter, which is a [[time-honoured]] ritual my mother learned from my grandmother.

questions.q: Do you think traditional culture is important?
questions.answer: Very much so. It gives people a sense of identity and connects generations. In a fast-changing world, I think [[preserving]] our traditions, our language and festivals especially, matters more than ever.

questions.q: Did your grandparents teach you about traditions?
questions.answer: Very much so, especially my grandmother. She has little formal education, but she's a [[treasure trove]] of folk tales, proverbs and old customs. Listening to her stories as a child gave me a real sense of where I come from.

questions.q: Do you ever wear traditional clothes?
questions.answer: Quite often, actually. I wear a panjabi at Eid, at weddings and on Pohela Boishakh. It's comfortable and elegant, and wearing it gives me a quiet sense of [[belonging]] to something bigger than myself.

questions.q: Do you think young people are losing interest in traditional culture?
questions.answer: To some extent, yes, mainly because of global influences and social media. But I don't think it's [[diminishing]] entirely. Many young people still take great pride in their roots, just alongside a more modern lifestyle.
